<challenge>
Design and build the strongest Gmail-inspired email application you can.

Recreate the clarity, information density, speed, and familiar workflows of a great modern inbox. Take the implementation as far as you can: choose the stack, scope, visual direction, data model, and technical limits that let you deliver the most convincing complete product.
</challenge>

<essential-outcomes>
The finished application must include:

- A polished, responsive mail shell with a recognizable inbox, navigation, toolbar, search, and account controls.
- A realistic seeded mailbox with varied senders, subjects, timestamps, labels, read states, attachments, threads, and message content.
- Functional mailbox navigation for at least Inbox, Starred, Sent, Drafts, and Trash.
- Working message selection, read/unread state, starring, archiving, deleting, and labeling.
- A usable search experience that filters or retrieves relevant mail.
- A message-reading view with a clear conversation hierarchy and useful actions.
- A compose experience with recipients, subject, body, draft behavior, send behavior, and a polished interaction model.
- Responsive behavior that remains coherent and usable on both desktop and mobile.
</essential-outcomes>

<product-depth>
Go beyond a static visual recreation. Interactions should update the interface consistently, preserve state where useful, and make the product feel alive. You may add keyboard shortcuts, bulk actions, category tabs, snoozing, scheduled mail, contact suggestions, rich composition, settings, themes, offline persistence, or any other details that strengthen the experience.

No external email account, authentication, paid service, or API key is required. A fully local product with excellent seeded data and convincing behavior is valid. Do not leave prominent controls as decorative placeholders when a meaningful local interaction can be implemented.
</product-depth>

<creative-freedom>
You have broad freedom over architecture, libraries, layout details, interaction design, copy, and visual polish. Use Gmail as the product reference, but make deliberate decisions and deliver a coherent application rather than a collection of disconnected screens.

Do not explain your design before building it. Make the product and engineering decisions yourself, implement the experience, test the important workflows, and refine it into the best result you can.
</creative-freedom>

<success-criteria>
The result should immediately read as a high-quality email client, reward exploration, and support a convincing end-to-end flow from finding a message to reading, organizing, composing, and sending mail. Visual fidelity matters, but functional depth, consistency, responsiveness, and product judgment matter just as much.
</success-criteria>

---
name: frontend-design
description: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.
license: Complete terms in LICENSE.txt
---

# Frontend Design

Approach this as the design lead at a small studio known for giving every client a visual identity that could not be mistaken for anyone else's. This client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view: make deliberate, opinionated choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this brief, and take one real aesthetic risk you can justify.

## Ground it in the subject

If the brief does not pin down what the product or subject is, pin it yourself before designing: name one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job, and state your choice. If there's any information in your memory about the human's preferences, context about what they're building, or designs you've made before – use that as a hint. The subject's own world, its materials, instruments, artifacts, and vernacular, is where distinctive choices come from. Build with the brief's real content and subject matter throughout.

## Design principles

For web designs, the hero is a thesis. Open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world, in whatever form makes sense for it: a headline, an image, an animation, a live demo, an interactive moment. Be deliberate with your choice: a big number with a small label, supporting stats, and a gradient accent is the template answer, only use if that's truly the best option.

Typography carries the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, not the same families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content.

Structure is information. Structural devices, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, should encode something true about the content, not decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence - like a real process or a typed timeline where order carries information the reader needs. Question if choices like numbered markers actually make sense before incorporating them.

Leverage motion deliberately. Think about where and if animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, a scroll-triggered reveal, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. An orchestrated moment usually lands harder than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation contributes to the feeling that the design is AI-generated.

Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.

Consider written content carefully. Often a design brief may not contain real content, and it's up to you to come up with copy. Copy can make a design feel as templated as the design itself. See the below section on writing for more guidance.

## Process: brainstorm, explore, plan, critique, build, critique again

For calibration: AI-generated design right now clusters around three looks: (1) a warm cream background (near #F4F1EA) with a high-contrast serif display and a terracotta accent; (2) a near-black background with a single bright acid-green or vermilion accent; (3) a broadsheet-style layout with hairline rules, zero border-radius, and dense newspaper-like columns. All three are legitimate for some briefs, but they are defaults rather than choices, and they appear regardless of subject. Where the brief pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — the brief's own words always win, including when it asks for one of these looks. Where it leaves an axis free, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults. Just like a human designer who's hired, there's often a careful balance between doing what you're good at and taking each project as a chance to experiment and learn.

Work in two passes. First, brainstorm a short design plan based on the human's design brief: create a compact token system with color, type, layout, and signature. Color: describe the palette as 4–6 named hex values. Type: the typefaces for 2+ roles (a characterful display face that's used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed). Layout: a layout concept, using one-sentence prose descriptions and ASCII wireframes to ideate and compare. Signature: the single unique element this page will be remembered by that embodies the brief in an appropriate way.

Then review that plan against the brief before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page (work through a similar prompt to see if you arrive somewhere similar) rather than a choice made for this specific brief — revise that part, say what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the relative uniqueness of your design plan should you start to write the code, following the revised plan exactly and deriving every color and type decision from it.

When writing the code, be careful of structuring your CSS selector specificities. It's easy to generate CSS classes that cancel each other out (especially with a type-based selector like .section and a element-based selector like .cta). This can happen often with paddings/margins between sections.

Try to do a lot of this planning and iteration in your thinking, and only show ideas to the user when you have higher confidence it'll delight them.

## Restraint and self-critique

Spend your boldness in one place. Let the signature element be the one memorable thing, keep everything around it quiet and disciplined, and cut any decoration that does not serve the brief. Not taking a risk can be a risk itself! Build to a quality floor without announcing it: responsive down to mobile, visible keyboard focus, reduced motion respected. Critique your own work as you build, taking screenshots if your environment supports it – a picture is worth 1000 tokens. Consider Chanel's advice: before leaving the house, take a look in the mirror and remove one accessory. Human creators have memory and always try to do something new, so if you have a space to quickly jot down notes about what you've tried, it can help you in future passes.

## More on writing in design

Words appear in a design for one reason: to make it easier to understand, and therefore easier to use. They are design material, not decoration. Bring the same intentionality to copy that you would bring to spacing and color. Before writing anything, ask what the design needs to say, and how it can best be said to help the person navigate the experience.

Write from the end user's side of the screen. Name things by what people control and recognize, never by how the system is built. A person manages notifications, not webhook config. Describe what something does in plain terms rather than selling it. Being specific is always better than being clever.

Use active voice as default. A control should say exactly what happens when it's used: "Save changes," not "Submit." An action keeps the same name through the whole flow, so the button that says "Publish" produces a toast that says "Published." The vocabulary of an interface is the signposting for someone navigating the product. Cohesion and consistency are how people learn their way around.

Treat failure and emptiness as moments for direction, not mood. Explain what went wrong and how to fix it, in the interface's voice rather than a person's. Errors don't apologize, and they are never vague about what happened. An empty screen is an invitation to act.

Keep the register conversational and tuned: plain verbs, sentence case, no filler, with tone matched to the brand and the audience. Let each element do exactly one job. A label labels, an example demonstrates, and nothing quietly does double duty.

# Product register

When design SERVES the product: app UIs, admin dashboards, settings panels, data tables, tools, authenticated surfaces, anything where the user is in a task.

## The product slop test

Not "would someone say AI made this." Familiarity is often a feature here. The test is: would a user fluent in the category's best tools (Linear, Figma, Notion, Raycast, Stripe come to mind) sit down and trust this interface, or pause at every subtly-off component?

Product UI's failure mode isn't flatness, it's strangeness without purpose: over-decorated buttons, mismatched form controls, gratuitous motion, display fonts where labels should be, invented affordances for standard tasks. The bar is earned familiarity. The tool should disappear into the task.

## Typography

- **One family is often right.** Product UIs don't need display/body pairing. A well-tuned sans carries headings, buttons, labels, body, data.
- **Fixed rem scale, not fluid.** Clamp-sized headings don't serve product UI. Users view at consistent DPI, and a fluid h1 that shrinks in a sidebar looks worse, not better.
- **Tighter scale ratio.** 1.125–1.2 between steps is typical. More type elements here than on brand surfaces; exaggerated contrast creates noise.
- **Line length still applies for prose** (65–75ch). Data and compact UI can run denser; tables at 120ch+ are fine.

## Color

Product defaults to Restrained. A single surface can earn Committed (a dashboard where one category color carries a report, an onboarding flow with a drenched welcome screen), but Restrained is the floor.

- State-rich semantic vocabulary: hover, focus, active, disabled, selected, loading, error, warning, success, info. Standardize these.
- Accent color used for primary actions, current selection, and state indicators only, not decoration.
- A second neutral layer for sidebars, toolbars, and panels (slightly cooler or warmer than the content surface).

## Layout

- Responsive behavior is structural (collapse sidebar, responsive table, breakpoint-driven columns), not fluid typography.

## Components

Every interactive component has: default, hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, error. Don't ship with half of these.

- Skeleton states for loading, not spinners in the middle of content.
- Empty states that teach the interface, not "nothing here."
- Consistent affordances across the surface. Same button shape. Same form-control vocabulary. Same icon style.

## Motion

- 150–250 ms on most transitions. Users are in flow; don't make them wait for choreography.
- Motion conveys state, not decoration. State change, feedback, loading, reveal: nothing else.
- No orchestrated page-load sequences. Product loads into a task; users don't want to watch it load.

## Product bans (on top of the shared absolute bans)

- Decorative motion that doesn't convey state.
- Inconsistent component vocabulary across screens. If the "save" button looks different in two places, one is wrong.
- Display fonts in UI labels, buttons, data.
- Reinventing standard affordances for flavor (custom scrollbars, weird form controls, non-standard modals).
- Heavy color or full-saturation accents on inactive states.
- Modal as first thought. Modals are usually laziness. Exhaust inline / progressive alternatives first.

## Product permissions

Product can afford things brand surfaces can't.

- System fonts and familiar sans defaults (Inter, SF Pro, system-ui stacks).
- Standard navigation patterns: top bar + side nav, breadcrumbs, tabs, command palettes.
- Density. Tables with many rows, panels with many labels, dense information when users need it.
- Consistency over surprise. The same visual vocabulary screen to screen is a virtue; delight is saved for moments, not pages.

# Web Interface Guidelines

Review files for compliance with Web Interface Guidelines.

## How It Works

1. Fetch the latest guidelines from the source URL below
2. Read the specified files (or prompt user for files/pattern)
3. Check against all rules in the fetched guidelines
4. Output findings in the terse `file:line` format

## Guidelines Source

Fetch fresh guidelines before each review:

```
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines/main/command.md
```

Use WebFetch to retrieve the latest rules. The fetched content contains all the rules and output format instructions.

## Usage

When a user provides a file or pattern argument:
1. Fetch guidelines from the source URL above
2. Read the specified files
3. Apply all rules from the fetched guidelines
4. Output findings using the format specified in the guidelines

If no files specified, ask the user which files to review.

export const SYS = {
  INBOX: 'INBOX',
  SENT: 'SENT',
  DRAFT: 'DRAFT',
  TRASH: 'TRASH',
  SPAM: 'SPAM',
  STARRED: 'STARRED',
  IMPORTANT: 'IMPORTANT',
  SNOOZED: 'SNOOZED',
  SCHEDULED: 'SCHEDULED',
} as const

export type SysLabel = (typeof SYS)[keyof typeof SYS]

export type Category = 'primary' | 'social' | 'promotions' | 'updates' | 'forums'

export type ViewKind =
  | 'inbox'
  | 'starred'
  | 'snoozed'
  | 'important'
  | 'sent'
  | 'scheduled'
  | 'drafts'
  | 'all'
  | 'spam'
  | 'trash'
  | 'label'
  | 'search'

export interface Contact {
  id: string
  name: string
  email: string
  hue: number
  title?: string
}

export type AttachmentKind = 'pdf' | 'image' | 'doc' | 'sheet' | 'slide' | 'zip' | 'code' | 'video'

export interface Attachment {
  id: string
  name: string
  kind: AttachmentKind
  size: number
  preview?: string
}

export interface Message {
  id: string
  threadId: string
  from: string
  to: string[]
  cc?: string[]
  bcc?: string[]
  date: number
  body: string
  attachments?: Attachment[]
  unread?: boolean
  draft?: boolean
  sendAt?: number
  inReplyTo?: string
}

export interface Thread {
  id: string
  subject: string
  messageIds: string[]
  labels: string[]
  category: Category
  snoozeUntil?: number
  lastActivity: number
}

export interface Label {
  id: string
  name: string
  color: string
  visible: boolean
}

export type Density = 'default' | 'comfortable' | 'compact'
export type ThemePref = 'light' | 'dark' | 'system'
export type ReadingPane = 'none' | 'right'

export interface Settings {
  theme: ThemePref
  density: Density
  readingPane: ReadingPane
  senderImages: boolean
  categoryTabs: boolean
  conversationView: boolean
  shortcuts: boolean
  undoSendSeconds: number
  snippets: boolean
  starredFirst: boolean
  signature: string
}

export interface ComposeWindow {
  id: string
  to: string[]
  cc: string[]
  bcc: string[]
  subject: string
  body: string
  attachments: Attachment[]
  threadId?: string
  inReplyTo?: string
  showCc: boolean
  showBcc: boolean
  sendAt?: number
  mode: 'normal' | 'minimized' | 'full'
  inline?: boolean
  kind: 'new' | 'reply' | 'replyAll' | 'forward' | 'draft'
}

export interface Snack {
  id: string
  text: string
  actionLabel?: string
  undo?: UndoEntry
  duration?: number
}

export type UndoEntry =
  | { type: 'labels'; snapshot: { threadId: string; labels: string[]; snoozeUntil?: number }[] }
  | { type: 'unread'; ids: string[]; unread: boolean }
  | { type: 'unsend'; messageId: string; threadId: string }
  | { type: 'restore'; threads: Thread[]; messages: Message[] }

export interface Account {
  name: string
  email: string
  hue: number
  storageUsedGb: number
  storageTotalGb: number
}

export interface Route {
  kind: ViewKind
  category?: Category
  labelId?: string
  query?: string
  threadId?: string
  page: number
}

export const PAGE_SIZE = 50

export const VIEW_TITLES: Record<ViewKind, string> = {
  inbox: 'Inbox',

+import { contactByEmail, ME } from './contacts'
+import { snippetFromHtml } from './format'
+import { SYS, type Category, type Message, type Thread, type ViewKind } from './types'
+
+export interface MailIndex {
+  threads: Thread[]
+  messages: Message[]
+}
+
+export function messagesOf(index: MailIndex, thread: Thread): Message[] {
+  const map = new Map(index.messages.map((m) => [m.id, m]))
+  return thread.messageIds.map((id) => map.get(id)).filter((m): m is Message => Boolean(m))
+}
+
+export function lastMessage(index: MailIndex, thread: Thread): Message | undefined {
+  const msgs = messagesOf(index, thread)
+  return msgs[msgs.length - 1]
+}
+
+export function threadUnread(index: MailIndex, thread: Thread): boolean {
+  return messagesOf(index, thread).some((m) => m.unread)
+}
+
+export function threadStarred(thread: Thread): boolean {
+  return thread.labels.includes(SYS.STARRED)
+}
+
+export function sendersLine(index: MailIndex, thread: Thread, me = ME.email): string {
+  const msgs = messagesOf(index, thread)
+  const names: string[] = []
+  const seen = new Set<string>()
+  for (const m of msgs) {
+    const key = m.from.toLowerCase()
+    if (seen.has(key)) continue
+    seen.add(key)
+    names.push(m.from.toLowerCase() === me.toLowerCase() ? 'me' : contactByEmail(m.from).name.split(' ')[0]!)
+  }
+  if (names.length <= 3) return names.join(', ')
+  return `${names.slice(0, 2).join(', ')} … ${names[names.length - 1]}`
+}
+
+export function matchesView(thread: Thread, kind: ViewKind, labelId?: string): boolean {
+  const L = thread.labels
+  const trashed = L.includes(SYS.TRASH)
+  const spam = L.includes(SYS.SPAM)
+  const draft = L.includes(SYS.DRAFT)
+  switch (kind) {
+    case 'inbox':
+      return L.includes(SYS.INBOX) && !trashed && !spam
+    case 'starred':
+      return L.includes(SYS.STARRED) && !trashed && !spam
+    case 'snoozed':
+      return L.includes(SYS.SNOOZED) && !trashed && !spam
+    case 'important':
+      return L.includes(SYS.IMPORTANT) && !trashed && !spam
+    case 'sent':
+      return L.includes(SYS.SENT) && !trashed && !spam && !draft
+    case 'scheduled':
+      return L.includes(SYS.SCHEDULED) && !trashed
+    case 'drafts':
+      return draft && !trashed && !L.includes(SYS.SCHEDULED)
+    case 'all':
+      return !trashed && !spam
+    case 'spam':
+      return spam && !trashed
+    case 'trash':
+      return trashed
+    case 'label':
+      return Boolean(labelId && L.includes(labelId) && !trashed && !spam)
+    case 'search':
+      return true
+  }
+}
+
+export interface ParsedQuery {
+  text: string[]
+  from?: string
+  to?: string
+  subject?: string
+  hasAttachment?: boolean
+  unread?: boolean
+  starred?: boolean
+  label?: string
+  in?: string
+}
+
+export function parseQuery(raw: string): ParsedQuery {
+  const q: ParsedQuery = { text: [] }
+  const re =
+    /(from|to|subject|label|in|is|has):(?:"([^"]+)"|(\S+))/gi
+  let rest = raw
+  let m: RegExpExecArray | null
+  const consumed: string[] = []
+  while ((m = re.exec(raw))) {
+    consumed.push(m[0])
+    const key = m[1]!.toLowerCase()
+    const val = (m[2] ?? m[3] ?? '').toLowerCase()
+    if (key === 'from') q.from = val
+    else if (key === 'to') q.to = val
+    else if (key === 'subject') q.subject = val
+    else if (key === 'label') q.label = val
+    else if (key === 'in') q.in = val
+    else if (key === 'is') {
+      if (val === 'unread') q.unread = true
+      if (val === 'read') q.unread = false
+      if (val === 'starred') q.starred = true
+    } else if (key === 'has' && val === 'attachment') q.hasAttachment = true
+  }
+  for (const c of consumed) rest = rest.replace(c, ' ')
+  q.text = rest.toLowerCase().split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean)
+  return q
+}
+
+function haystack(index: MailIndex, thread: Thread): string {
+  const msgs = messagesOf(index, thread)
+  const bits = [
+    thread.subject,
+    ...msgs.flatMap((m) => [
+      m.from,
+      ...m.to,
+      ...(m.cc ?? []),
+      contactByEmail(m.from).name,
+      snippetFromHtml(m.body, 2000),
+      ...(m.attachments?.map((a) => a.name) ?? []),
+    ]),
+  ]
+  return bits.join(' ').toLowerCase()
+}
+
+export function searchThreads(index: MailIndex, raw: string): Thread[] {
+  const q = parseQuery(raw)
+  return index.threads.filter((t) => {
+    const msgs = messagesOf(index, t)
+    if (q.from && !msgs.some((m) => m.from.toLowerCase().includes(q.from!) || contactByEmail(m.from).name.toLowerCase().includes(q.from!)))
+      return false
+    if (q.to && !msgs.some((m) => [...m.to, ...(m.cc ?? [])].some((e) => e.toLowerCase().includes(q.to!) || contactByEmail(e).name.toLowerCase().includes(q.to!))))
+      return false
+    if (q.subject && !t.subject.toLowerCase().includes(q.subject)) return false
+    if (q.hasAttachment && !msgs.some((m) => (m.attachments?.length ?? 0) > 0)) return false
+    if (q.unread === true && !threadUnread(index, t)) return false
+    if (q.unread === false && threadUnread(index, t)) return false
+    if (q.starred && !t.labels.includes(SYS.STARRED)) return false
+    if (q.label && !t.labels.some((id) => id.toLowerCase().includes(q.label!) || id === q.label)) {
+      return false
+    }
+    if (q.in) {
+      const map: Record<string, ViewKind> = {
+        inbox: 'inbox',
+        starred: 'starred',
+        snoozed: 'snoozed',
+        sent: 'sent',
+        drafts: 'drafts',
+        trash: 'trash',
+        spam: 'spam',
+        scheduled: 'scheduled',
+      }
+      const kind = map[q.in]
+      if (kind && !matchesView(t, kind)) return false
+    }
+    if (q.text.length && !q.text.every((w) => haystack(index, t).includes(w))) return false
+    return true
+  })
+}
+
+export function unreadCount(
+  index: MailIndex,
+  kind: ViewKind,
+  labelId?: string,
+  category?: Category,
+): number {
+  return index.threads.filter((t) => {
+    if (!matchesView(t, kind, labelId)) return false
+    if (category && t.category !== category) return false
+    return threadUnread(index, t)
+  }).length
+}
+
+export function draftCount(index: MailIndex): number {
+  return index.threads.filter((t) => matchesView(t, 'drafts')).length
+}

+import { createContext, useCallback, useContext, useEffect, useMemo, useState, type ReactNode } from 'react'
+import { draftCount, matchesView, searchThreads, threadUnread, unreadCount } from './search'
+import { draftCompose, newCompose, useDispatch, useIndex, useStore } from './store'
+import {
+  PAGE_SIZE,
+  type Category,
+  type Route,
+  type ViewKind,
+} from './types'
+
+export type DialogKind =
+  | { kind: 'none' }
+  | { kind: 'settings' }
+  | { kind: 'shortcuts' }
+  | { kind: 'labels' }
+  | { kind: 'snooze'; ids: string[] }
+  | { kind: 'schedule'; composeId: string }
+  | { kind: 'newLabel'; ids: string[] }
+
+interface AppApi {
+  route: Route
+  navigate: (r: Partial<Route> & { kind: ViewKind }) => void
+  openThread: (id: string | undefined) => void
+  sidebarOpen: boolean
+  setSidebarOpen: (v: boolean) => void
+  railCollapsed: boolean
+  toggleRail: () => void
+  dialog: DialogKind
+  setDialog: (d: DialogKind) => void
+  searchOpen: boolean
+  setSearchOpen: (v: boolean) => void
+  visibleThreads: ReturnType<typeof useVisible>['threads']
+  total: number
+  pageCount: number
+  unreadInbox: number
+  drafts: number
+  openCompose: () => void
+  openDraft: (threadId: string) => void
+}
+
+const AppCtx = createContext<AppApi | null>(null)
+
+function parseHash(): Route {
+  const h = window.location.hash.replace(/^#\/?/, '')
+  const [path, qs] = h.split('?')
+  const params = new URLSearchParams(qs ?? '')
+  const parts = (path ?? '').split('/').filter(Boolean)
+  const page = Math.max(0, Number(params.get('p') ?? 0) || 0)
+  const threadIdx = parts.indexOf('t')
+  const threadId = threadIdx >= 0 ? parts[threadIdx + 1] : params.get('t') ?? undefined
+  const kindPart = parts[0] || 'inbox'
+  const category = parts[1] && ['primary', 'social', 'promotions', 'updates', 'forums'].includes(parts[1])
+    ? (parts[1] as Category)
+    : undefined
+
+  if (kindPart === 'search') {
+    return { kind: 'search', query: params.get('q') ?? '', threadId, page }
+  }
+  if (kindPart === 'label') {
+    return { kind: 'label', labelId: parts[1], threadId, page }
+  }
+  const kinds: ViewKind[] = [
+    'inbox', 'starred', 'snoozed', 'important', 'sent', 'scheduled', 'drafts', 'all', 'spam', 'trash',
+  ]
+  const kind = kinds.includes(kindPart as ViewKind) ? (kindPart as ViewKind) : 'inbox'
+  return { kind, category: kind === 'inbox' ? category : undefined, threadId, page }
+}
+
+function toHash(r: Route): string {
+  const params = new URLSearchParams()
+  if (r.kind === 'search') params.set('q', r.query ?? '')
+  if (r.page) params.set('p', String(r.page))
+  let path = r.kind
+  if (r.kind === 'inbox' && r.category && r.category !== 'primary') path += `/${r.category}`
+  if (r.kind === 'label' && r.labelId) path += `/${r.labelId}`
+  if (r.threadId) path += `/t/${r.threadId}`
+  const q = params.toString()
+  return `#/${path}${q ? `?${q}` : ''}`
+}
+
+function useVisible(route: Route) {
+  const index = useIndex()
+  const settings = useStore().settings
+  return useMemo(() => {
+    let threads =
+      route.kind === 'search'
+        ? searchThreads(index, route.query ?? '')
+        : index.threads.filter((t) => matchesView(t, route.kind, route.labelId))
+    if (route.kind === 'inbox' && route.category) {
+      threads = threads.filter((t) => t.category === route.category)
+    }
+    threads = [...threads].sort((a, b) => b.lastActivity - a.lastActivity)
+    if (settings.starredFirst) {
+      threads.sort((a, b) => Number(a.labels.includes('STARRED') === false) - Number(b.labels.includes('STARRED') === false) || b.lastActivity - a.lastActivity)
+    }
+    const total = threads.length
+    const start = route.page * PAGE_SIZE
+    return { threads: threads.slice(start, start + PAGE_SIZE), total, all: threads }
+  }, [index, route, settings.starredFirst])
+}
+
+export function AppProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
+  const [route, setRoute] = useState<Route>(() => (typeof window === 'undefined' ? { kind: 'inbox', page: 0 } : parseHash()))
+  const [sidebarOpen, setSidebarOpen] = useState(false)
+  const [railCollapsed, setRailCollapsed] = useState(false)
+  const [dialog, setDialog] = useState<DialogKind>({ kind: 'none' })
+  const [searchOpen, setSearchOpen] = useState(false)
+  const store = useStore()
+  const dispatch = useDispatch()
+  const visible = useVisible(route)
+  const index = useIndex()
+
+  useEffect(() => {
+    const onHash = () => setRoute(parseHash())
+    window.addEventListener('hashchange', onHash)
+    if (!window.location.hash) window.location.hash = '/inbox'
+    return () => window.removeEventListener('hashchange', onHash)
+  }, [])
+
+  const navigate = useCallback((r: Partial<Route> & { kind: ViewKind }) => {
+    const next: Route = { page: 0, ...r }
+    window.location.hash = toHash(next)
+    setSidebarOpen(false)
+  }, [])
+
+  const openThread = useCallback(
+    (id: string | undefined) => {
+      const next = { ...route, threadId: id }
+      window.location.hash = toHash(next)
+    },
+    [route],
+  )
+
+  const openCompose = useCallback(() => {
+    dispatch({ t: 'openCompose', compose: newCompose() })
+  }, [dispatch])
+
+  const openDraft = useCallback(
+    (threadId: string) => {
+      const thread = store.threads.find((t) => t.id === threadId)
+      if (!thread) return
+      dispatch({ t: 'openCompose', compose: draftCompose(thread, store.messages) })
+    },
+    [dispatch, store.messages, store.threads],

+
+export function useShortcuts() {
+  const app = useApp()
+  const store = useStore()
+  const dispatch = useDispatch()
+  const index = useIndex()
+  const chord = useRef('')
+
+  useEffect(() => {
+    if (!store.settings.shortcuts) return
+
+    const onKey = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
+      const t = e.target as HTMLElement
+      const typing = t.tagName === 'INPUT' || t.tagName === 'TEXTAREA' || t.isContentEditable
+      if (e.key === 'Escape') {
+        if (app.dialog.kind !== 'none') app.setDialog({ kind: 'none' })
+        else if (store.compose.length) dispatch({ t: 'closeCompose', id: store.compose[store.compose.length - 1]!.id })
+        else if (app.route.threadId) app.openThread(undefined)
+        else dispatch({ t: 'clearSelect' })
+        return
+      }
+      if (typing) return
+      if (e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey || e.altKey) return
+
+      const key = e.key
+      if (key === '?') {
+        e.preventDefault()
+        app.setDialog({ kind: 'shortcuts' })
+        return
+      }
+      if (key === '/') {
+        e.preventDefault()
+        document.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('input[aria-label="Search mail"]')?.focus()
+        return
+      }
+      if (key === 'c') {
+        e.preventDefault()
+        app.openCompose()
+        return
+      }
+
+      if (chord.current === 'g') {
+        chord.current = ''
+        if (key === 'i') app.navigate({ kind: 'inbox' })
+        if (key === 's') app.navigate({ kind: 'starred' })
+        if (key === 't') app.navigate({ kind: 'sent' })
+        if (key === 'd') app.navigate({ kind: 'drafts' })
+        return
+      }
+      if (key === 'g') {
+        chord.current = 'g'
+        window.setTimeout(() => {
+          chord.current = ''
+        }, 700)
+        return
+      }
+
+      const list = app.visibleThreads
+      const currentId = app.route.threadId ?? store.lastSelectedId ?? list[0]?.id
+      const idx = list.findIndex((t) => t.id === currentId)
+      const ids = store.selectedIds.length ? store.selectedIds : currentId ? [currentId] : []
+      const thread = store.threads.find((t) => t.id === (app.route.threadId ?? currentId))
+      const last = thread ? lastMessage(index, thread) : undefined
+
+      if (key === 'j') {
+        const n = list[Math.min(list.length - 1, idx + 1)]
+        if (n) {
+          if (app.route.threadId) app.openThread(n.id)
+          else dispatch({ t: 'select', ids: [n.id] })
+        }
+      }
+      if (key === 'k') {
+        const n = list[Math.max(0, idx - 1)]
+        if (n) {
+          if (app.route.threadId) app.openThread(n.id)
+          else dispatch({ t: 'select', ids: [n.id] })
+        }
+      }
+      if (key === 'o' || key === 'Enter') {
+        if (currentId) app.openThread(currentId)
+      }
+      if (key === 'u') app.openThread(undefined)
+      if (key === 'e' && ids.length) dispatch({ t: 'archive', ids })
+      if (key === '#' && ids.length) dispatch({ t: 'trash', ids })
+      if (key === 's' && ids.length) {
+        const starred = thread?.labels.includes('STARRED')
+        dispatch({ t: 'star', ids, starred: !starred })
+      }
+      if (key === 'x' && currentId) dispatch({ t: 'toggleSelect', id: currentId })
+      if (key === 'r' && thread && last) dispatch({ t: 'openCompose', compose: replyCompose(thread, last, false) })
+      if (key === 'a' && thread && last) dispatch({ t: 'openCompose', compose: replyCompose(thread, last, true) })
+      if (key === 'f' && thread && last) dispatch({ t: 'openCompose', compose: forwardCompose(thread, last) })
+      if (key === 'I' && ids.length) dispatch({ t: 'markRead', ids, unread: false })
+      if (key === 'U' && ids.length) dispatch({ t: 'markRead', ids, unread: true })
+    }
+
+    window.addEventListener('keydown', onKey)
+    return () => window.removeEventListener('keydown', onKey)
+  }, [app, dispatch, index, store])

## React Compiler

The React Compiler is not enabled on this template because of its impact on dev & build performances. To add it, see [this documentation](https://react.dev/learn/react-compiler/installation).

## Expanding the Oxlint configuration

If you are developing a production application, we recommend enabling type-aware lint rules by installing `oxlint-tsgolint` and editing `.oxlintrc.json`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "./node_modules/oxlint/configuration_schema.json",
  "plugins": ["react", "typescript", "oxc"],
  "options": {
    "typeAware": true
  },
  "rules": {
    "react/rules-of-hooks": "error",
    "react/only-export-components": ["warn", { "allowConstantExport": true }]
  }
}
```
